validity.recommendation: No merge needed. Keep P7458 and P7450 as separate rows -- they are two distinct physical pipelines that happen to both carry the word 'Beluga'.
validity.researcher_notes: ORCHESTRATOR-ASSIGNED ADJUDICATION: is P7458 (PipelineName 'Beluga Pipeline', blank SegmentName, 101.35 mi, 20-in, operating, row 3844) a duplicate of P7450 (PipelineName 'Kenai Beluga Pipeline', SegmentName 'Beluga Pipeline', 16.21 mi, no diameter, operating, row 3836)? VERDICT: NOT A DUPLICATE -- negative verdict, two distinct facilities. Evidence, four independent origins: (1) Alaska DEC APDES Pipeline GP Fact Sheet (dec.alaska.gov/media/mxmbp1n0/akg320000_fs_vfinal.pdf) has a dedicated subsection 'Beluga Natural Gas Transmission Pipeline' stating verbatim: 'The Beluga Power Plant Pipeline was built in 1984 and is owned and operated by ENSTAR Natural Gas Company. The Beluga Natural Gas Transmission Pipeline is a 20-inch diameter pipeline that supplies gas from the Beluga Power Plant to residential and commercial customers in Anchorage.' The SAME fact sheet, in its Hilcorp/Tyonek subsection, separately refers to 'the Beluga Pipeline section of Kenai Beluga Pipeline System' as the destination where Tyonek-area gas enters -- explicitly naming P7450's system as a DIFFERENT facility from ENSTAR's line. (2) Alaska DNR Donlin Gold special-area permit (dnr.alaska.gov/mlw/mining/large-mines/donlin/pdf/fh21-spo-044-sa.pdf) independently describes 'the existing ENSTAR 20-inch Beluga natural gas pipeline (BPL)' as the tie-in point for the proposed Donlin lateral -- again ENSTAR, 20-inch, matching P7458 exactly. (3) ConocoPhillips Alaska's Cook Inlet history timeline (conocophillipsalaska.com/ea/cookinlettimeline/) states twice, independently of DEC/DNR: 'In 1984, ENSTAR Natural Gas Company constructed a pipeline from Anchorage to the Beluga River Gas Field' -- confirms owner, year, and route for P7458 specifically. (4) The Regulatory Commission of Alaska's public notice for Docket P-14-025 (aws.state.ak.us/OnlinePublicNotices/Notices/View.aspx?id=174074, 2014) documents that 'Kenai Beluga Pipeline, LLC (KBPL), Beluga Pipeline Company (Beluga), Kenai Kachemak Pipeline, LLC (KKPL), Hilcorp Alaska, LLC d/b/a Cook Inlet Gas Gathering System (CIGGS), and Hilcorp Alaska, LLC d/b/a Kenai Nikiski Pipeline (KNPL)... are all owned 100 percent, directly or indirectly, by Hilcorp Alaska, LLC' and were consolidated into one CPCN (No. 668) under KBPL -- i.e., the corporate entity actually named 'Beluga Pipeline Company' is a wholly Hilcorp-owned entity, structurally and historically unrelated to ENSTAR. (5) PHMSA Final Order CPF No. 5-2021-023-NOPV (2022-03-28, against Harvest Alaska LLC) separately discusses a bi-directional 'Beluga Transmission Pipeline' at Kaloa Junction tied to the Beluga River Unit (BRU) and 'West CIGGS' sources -- consistent with the Hilcorp/Harvest-side KBPL 'Beluga Pipeline' segment (P7450), not ENSTAR's line. CONCLUSION: P7458 = ENSTAR's own 'Beluga Natural Gas Transmission Pipeline' / 'Beluga Power Plant Pipeline' (Beluga Power Plant -> Anchorage, 20-in, built 1984, 100% ENSTAR-owned). P7450 = the former 'Beluga Pipeline Company' segment of the Hilcorp-owned, consolidated Kenai Beluga Pipeline System (KBPL, near Kaloa Junction on the west side of Cook Inlet), unrelated in ownership, history, or route to P7458. Both rows should stand as-is; no merge, no relabel. LENGTH PLAUSIBILITY (also orchestrator-flagged): 101.35 mi is plausible despite the Beluga field sitting only ~40 mi west of Anchorage across the inlet, because ENSTAR's route does not cross the inlet directly -- it runs north and east around the head of Cook Inlet along the coast. Internal (uncitable, GOIT-GGIT-pipeline-routes repo) geometry check on P7458.geojson (127-point MultiLineString) sums to ~101.24 mi via haversine, closely matching the recorded 101.35 mi and confirming the routing explanation; this is our own measurement, not a citable second source, and is not staged as a proposed_ref for the Length unit (see fills[] Length record, which remains UNRESOLVED for an independent PUBLISHED mileage figure).

validity.recommendation: Correct Operator from 'Alaska Pipeline Co LLC' to 'ENSTAR Natural Gas Company'.
validity.researcher_notes: The sheet's Operator value 'Alaska Pipeline Co LLC' has no ref and no independent source was found naming it as this pipeline's operator. Both independent state-agency sources that describe this pipeline directly state ENSTAR operates it: DEC's fact sheet says verbatim 'is owned and operated by ENSTAR Natural Gas Company' and DNR's Donlin permit calls it 'the existing ENSTAR 20-inch Beluga natural gas pipeline (BPL)'. Searched for 'Alaska Pipeline Co' / 'Alaska Pipeline Company' via SEC EDGAR full-text search: found one real, verifiable entity by that name in a 2003 SEMCO Energy 10-K exhibit (SEC EDGAR accession 0000950124-06-001183, exhibit 10.27) -- 'Alaska Pipeline Company' (APC) was a party to a Cook Inlet gas sales/purchase contract for Moquawkie-field gas, corresponding with ENSTAR's 'Kuparuk and Cook Inlet Business Group'. This confirms APC was a real Cook Inlet gas-marketing entity circa 2000-2003, but nothing in that filing or elsewhere ties APC to operating the physical Beluga-to-Anchorage transmission pipeline -- it reads as a gas commodity counterparty, not a pipeline operator of record, and is a different name from 'Beluga Pipeline Company' (the actual historical Hilcorp-side entity documented in the RCA P-14-025 notice, see the duplicate validity record above). Also attempted: Regulatory Commission of Alaska pipeline-carrier pages (rca.alaska.gov) and Alaska Division of Corporations entity search (commerce.alaska.gov) -- both returned HTTP 403 on every route tried (WebFetch and curl, multiple user agents); Google and DuckDuckGo web search returned JS-challenge walls; Bing HTML search returned only generic Alaska tourism/Wikipedia results for queries containing 'Alaska Pipeline Company/Co' specifically (root cause undiagnosed) while differently-worded queries returned normal results, suggesting a query-specific degradation rather than a total block. No source was found supporting 'Alaska Pipeline Co LLC' as this pipeline's operator; two independent, directly-on-point state agency sources instead name ENSTAR Natural Gas Company as owner AND operator.

cross_row_leads.facts: RCA Docket P-14-025 (2014) notice: 'Kenai Beluga Pipeline, LLC (KBPL), Beluga Pipeline Company (Beluga), Kenai Kachemak Pipeline, LLC (KKPL), Hilcorp Alaska, LLC d/b/a Cook Inlet Gas Gathering System (CIGGS), and Hilcorp Alaska, LLC d/b/a Kenai Nikiski Pipeline (KNPL)...are all owned 100 percent, directly or indirectly, by Hilcorp Alaska, LLC' and were consolidated into a single CPCN No. 668 with KBPL as operator of the consolidated system (CIPL/CIGGS/KKPL/KNPL CPCNs 448, 711, 689 returned). The corporate entity actually named 'Beluga Pipeline Company' is this Hilcorp-side entity -- directly relevant to P7450's Operator/Owner and to distinguishing it from P7458 (ENSTAR's separate Beluga Natural Gas Transmission Pipeline).

PHMSA Final Order, CPF No. 5-2021-023-NOPV, dated 2022-03-28, against Harvest Alaska, LLC, describes a bi-directional 'Beluga Transmission Pipeline' at Kaloa Junction, tied to the Beluga River Unit (BRU) and 'West CIGGS' gas sources, with PSV-10056/PSV-002/PSV X-028 as key safety equipment and an ILI run in July 2019 -- physical/operational detail for P7450's segment, plus confirms Harvest Alaska as current operator.

Fact sheet's 'Tyonek Natural Gas Pipeline' subsection: 8-mile 10-inch line KPL Junction->Halbouty Hill; 22.5-mile 16-inch Halbouty Station->Moose Point; dual 12.89-mile 10-inch submarine lines Moose Point->offshore Tyonek Production Platform; 7.5-mile 10-inch line Tyonek Platform->Ladd Landing (west side of Upper Cook Inlet), feeding into 'the Beluga Pipeline section of Kenai Beluga Pipeline System'. Segment-level mileage/diameter detail potentially relevant to P7455 (Cook Inlet Gas Gathering System, Tyonek Area).

Fact sheet's 'Hilcorp Pipeline System' subsection: Swanson River Unit (SRU) pipeline is 18.8 miles, 16-inch, Swanson River Field -> Kenai Pipeline Company Junction; also describes BRU produced-water lines, Kenai Gas Field (KGF) 12/16/20/24-inch gathering lines, and the buried 10-inch Seaview Gas Pipeline (Seaview Pad -> ENSTAR tie-in valve). Potentially relevant to P7453 (Kenai Nikiski Pipeline) spec detail.

Donlin Gold special-area permit gives a more precise length than DEC's ~315 mi: 'approximately 315.9 miles' for the proposed 14-inch lateral from the existing ENSTAR 20-inch BPL tie-in point to the mine site, under ROW lease ADL 231908. Confirms/refines P2526's recorded len=315.0 dia=14.00.

'Potential Future Pipelines' section: 'The Alaska Liquefied Natural Gas (AK LNG) Pipeline is a potential new 42-inch diameter and 800-mile long natural gas pipeline from the North Slope to Cook Inlet...begins at a Gas Treatment Plant located in Prudhoe Bay and terminate at a proposed Liquefaction Facility in Nikiski, Alaska (AK LNG Project, 2014).' Corroborates P0147's recorded len=807 dia=42 (~800 mi, close agreement).

status_reviews.researcher_notes: Recorded Status=operating is still correct. Most recent independent evidence dates to approximately 2023 (DEC's reissued Pipeline GP fact sheet, whose underlying discharge-monitoring data tables run through December 2022 and which describes the ENSTAR Beluga line as a current, active permittee); the 2021 DNR Donlin permit and ConocoPhillips Alaska's Cook Inlet history page (undated but describing ENSTAR's continuing residential/commercial gas supply to Anchorage) are consistent. No evidence of shutdown, decommissioning, or ownership change was found in any source reviewed (DEC, DNR, ConocoPhillips, PHMSA, RCA notice). No newer dated evidence than 2023 was located; searches for recent (2024-2026) Alaska press coverage of ENSTAR's Beluga line returned nothing specific to this pipeline (only routine ENSTAR/Cook Inlet gas-supply-shortage coverage unrelated to this facility's operational status).

summary: P7458 (ENSTAR's Beluga Natural Gas Transmission Pipeline, Beluga->Anchorage, 1984, 20-in) confirmed NOT a duplicate of P7450 (Hilcorp/KBPL's separate 'Beluga Pipeline Company' segment near Kaloa Junction) via 4 independent sources (DEC, DNR, RCA, PHMSA); Operator corrected from unsourced 'Alaska Pipeline Co LLC' to ENSTAR Natural Gas Company (attribution concern); Status/Fuel/PipelineType/Start/Diameter/FuelSource/Location/Owner re-sourced with independent refs; Length, Capacity, Pressure, Proposal, SegmentCost left UNRESOLVED (no published source found, though Length's 101.35 mi is corroborated by an internal, uncitable route-geometry check).
